atoms.b: One of the Vikings still ((raving ++raiding)) was called Rollo. After a failed attempt to raid Paris, he made a treaty with the French king, who let Rollo settle in Normandy.

atoms.text: By the 10th century, Vikings in Scandinavia had started to convert to Christianity. However, not all leaders took the same approach to converting their people.

Harald Bluetooth was the King of Denmark from AD 958-985. He wished for the people of Denmark to convert to Christianity, but he left the choice up to them. In AD 960, he showed his commitment to his faith by putting up a runestone with a figure of Jesus on it.

Olaf Tryggvason was a Viking warrior who got baptised in England. In AD 995, he became King of Norway and built the first Christian church there. Unlike Harald Bluetooth, Olaf used force to convert his people.
